pharm: Selective progestogen that induces a hypoestrogenic, hyperprogestogenic local environment causing decidualization and atrophy of endometrial tissue; used for endometriosis
quick: With or without food, same time daily
Contraindicated in active/severe liver disease or tumor
BP, bleeding pattern, mood, bone health (long-term)
summary: Dienogest is a selective progestogen with antiandrogenic and only weak antigonadotropic activity, given as a 2 mg once-daily tablet for the treatment of endometriosis. It produces a local hypoestrogenic, hyperprogestogenic environment that decidualizes and then atrophies endometriotic tissue, reducing pelvic pain. Unlike danazol or GnRH agonists it has a favourable estrogen profile with modest effects on bone, but it commonly causes irregular bleeding, especially early in treatment. As monotherapy it is approved in Europe and many other regions but is not FDA-approved in the United States (where dienogest is available only in combined oral contraceptives such as Natazia).
indications: Component of some combined oral contraceptives (with estradiol valerate)

dosage.d: 2 mg once daily, taken continuously without a break
dosage.n: Start on any day of the cycle; take at about the same time each day

dosage.c: Missed/late by >12 h, vomiting or diarrhea
dosage.d: Take next tablet as usual; efficacy may be reduced for that day
dosage.n: Use additional precautions if also relied on for contraception

admin: Take one tablet daily at about the same time, continuously, with or without food
Bleeding may be irregular, especially in the first months - continue therapy
If a dose is missed by more than 12 hours, take the next tablet at the usual time
moa: A potent progestogen that binds progesterone receptors, inducing decidualization followed by atrophy of endometrial and endometriotic tissue. It moderately reduces ovarian estradiol production and has antiandrogenic activity, creating a local hypoestrogenic, hyperprogestogenic milieu that suppresses the growth of endometriotic lesions and associated pain.

absolute: Current or history of arterial or cardiovascular disease (e.g. MI, stroke, angina)
Severe hepatic disease or history of liver tumor

preg: Contraindicated. Dienogest should not be used during pregnancy; exclude pregnancy before starting and discontinue if pregnancy occurs.
lact: Not recommended. Hormones may pass into breast milk; a decision should be made to discontinue breastfeeding or the drug, weighing benefit to the child and the mother.
renal: No specific data in renal impairment; use with caution.
hepatic: Contraindicated in severe or active hepatic disease and in current or past liver tumors. Caution and clinical judgement are needed in milder hepatic impairment.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St John's wort) - reduced dienogest efficacy
HIV/HCV protease inhibitors and NNRTIs - variable effects on progestogen levels
moderate: CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, erythromycin, clarithromycin) - increased dienogest exposure
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food
interactions.diagnostics: May affect liver, thyroid, adrenal and renal function laboratory parameters and coagulation/fibrinolysis tests

serious: Significant changes in bone mineral density with prolonged use

monitoring: Bone mineral density with long-term use
counsel: Take one tablet daily at the same time, continuously, even during bleeding
Irregular bleeding is common, especially in the first months
This is not a reliable contraceptive on its own - use non-hormonal contraception if needed
Report severe leg pain/swelling, chest pain, shortness of breath, or sudden severe headache
Tell your doctor if you develop low mood or have a history of depression
Avoid St John's wort and tell your doctor about other medicines
pk: Symptom improvement over weeks; amenorrhea often within months
pearls: Not FDA-approved as monotherapy; EU/SmPC-approved for endometriosis at 2 mg daily (US has dienogest only in combination OCs)
More favourable estrogen and bone profile than GnRH agonists or danazol
Irregular bleeding is the most common reason for discontinuation - counsel proactively
Take continuously without a pill-free interval
Efficacy can be reduced by CYP3A4-inducing drugs
missed: If less than 24 hours late, take the missed tablet as soon as remembered and the next at the usual time. If more than 24 hours, skip the missed dose and continue; efficacy may be reduced and breakthrough bleeding may occur.
overdose: No serious harmful effects from overdose are expected; possible nausea, vomiting or withdrawal/irregular bleeding. There is no specific antidote; management is supportive.
